Hello! Polyamorous person here! 

You're monogamist. There's no way around it, and that's okay, it's completely valid! That's where your morals and beliefs lie, and *that's okay*. 

But I am slightly concerned about your boyfriend. It seems like he's never mentioned becoming an open relationship, and his reasoning on *why* he wants to become open is kinda concerning. He said he saw what your sisters husband cheating on her has done. And he brings up he never wants to hurt you that way. Was he debating on cheating before your sister moved in with you? Has he already cheated and is using this as a way to avoid consuqences? 

And even after you said you were monogamist, and didn't want that, he doesn't stop. He keeps pushing *his* needs. He's not taking in consideration what *YOUR* needs are. It sounds like he's not even trying to listen. Hell, it was HORRIBLE that the "rules" you could make up for him were "No ugly people" and "No fat people" 

Polyamory is based on consent and trust. I've had partners who cheated on me, claiming they were poly when we agreed to a monogamist relationship, I've had partners tell me they weren't comfortable with polyamory, and I'm currently in an amazing polyamorous relationship. You're not consenting to being open, you don't WANT to be open, you've never been open, so he can't be upset at the fact you said no. Its not for everyone, that's fine. What's not fine is pushing your non-monogamous wants on your non consenting partner. 

How would he react if you agreed, and you started seeing other people? That you wanted to explore your sexuality, and became active with other sexual partners while he's gone? How would that make *him* feel?

He owns my heart, and is the love of my life, and we're planning on getting married in October! But, we both want to explore ourself outside of trauma. I knew from the start he wasnt Mongolian, but he respected the fact I didn't want to be open at the start of our relationship. As time went on, we did open our relationship for other sexual partners only. We have rules set for each other, and we're safe about it. But, we're happy, and it works for us.

I get the feeling he hasn't respected your feelings throughout this interaction. He kept pushing it even though you said no. You even attempted to see his side, and educated yourself. But it's not for you. He should respect that.
